newsitem.title: SWEDEN: OLYMPICS-Swedes say 'yes' to 2004 Olympics in 11th-hour poll.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-Swedes say 'yes' to 2004 Olympics in 11th-hour poll.

text.p: Swedes have come out in favour of hosting the 2004 Olympics in Stockholm after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) criticised Sweden for not wanting the games, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
A survey of 1,000 Swedes by pollster IMU and tabloid newspaper Aftonbladet, showed 46 percent of Swedes were now in favour of hosting the Olympics, outranking those against for the first time.

A total of 43 percent still remained opposed to hosting the games but this had fallen from 52 percent of 1,100 people surveyed in September last year. At that time only 20 percent of Swedes wanted the Olympics.
But with Olympic chiefs set to draw up their shortlist of candidates to host the 2004 Olympics this Thursday in Lausanne, the swing in public opinion could have come too late.

"This was the only point on which we did not score well according to the IOC's selection committee," Ingvar Carlsson, chairman of the Stockholm 2004 foundation and former Swedish prime minister, told Aftonbladet.
"This has changed dramatically...and I feel the wind is now blowing strongly in our direction."

The 11 cities vying to stage the games will present their bids to the IOC this week before officials throw out the weakest on Friday and name the four, or probably five, candidates who will go forward to a September vote.

It looks as though Athens, Rome, Buenos Aires, Cape Town and Stockholm will stay in the running while Istanbul, Lille, Rio de Janeiro, San Juan, Seville and St Petersburg are likely to be turned down.
Stockholm was regarded as having one of the strongest technical bids as far as facilities and organisation were concerned but local opposition was considered a problem.
